candidates.topic: Mayo Clinic PATHFINDER2 multi-cancer early detection blood test detects 17 cancer types
candidates.recommended_angle: Move past the 'multi-cancer detection' headline to actual performance data — sensitivity/specificity by cancer type, false-positive rate, and who should realistically ask their doctor about it.
candidates.why_now: Mayo Clinic just published new prospective-study results specifying the blood test detected 17 distinct cancer types — a concrete new data point beyond the general 'evaluates performance and safety' framing already covered this week (09/23).
candidates.primary_headline: Mayo Clinic Study: New Blood Test Detected 17 Types of Cancer Early — What the Data Actually Shows
candidates.next_steps: Assign P2 brief today; full deep-dive with Mayo Clinic investigator quote and sensitivity/specificity breakdown.
integrity_flags: This is a prospective screening-performance study, not evidence the test improves survival or outcomes — those trial arms take years to mature. Do not imply mortality benefit.
Report sensitivity/specificity and false-positive rate explicitly; avoid 'detects cancer' framing without those numbers.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Moderate trend (58) driven by new institutional primary-source data point released this week with 17-cancer-type specificity; not front-page velocity but clear news peg.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: 72 score reflects evaluative search intent fit ('does this test work'), named entity (PATHFINDER2), and strong internal-linking potential to cancer-screening guidance cluster.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Named entity, maps to natural query 'how accurate is the multi-cancer blood test,' institutional primary source — solid AI-citation potential.
candidates.notes: Institutional primary source (Mayo Clinic News Network) passes Skill 02b. Estimated word count 900–1100. Visual: simple infographic on liquid biopsy mechanism and cancer-type breakdown chart.

issues: The evidence (Mayo Clinic News Network item) describes the study only as a 'large prospective study' and does not name it 'PATHFINDER 2' — that specific trial identifier is not confirmed by the collected evidence.

The 'why now' references prior coverage from 09/23 framing the study as 'evaluates performance and safety,' which is not present in the evidence provided; only the 09/22 Mayo Clinic item is available.
